name.text: Finding the smallest integer satisfying a linear inequality

questiontext.text:
(a) Solve the following inequality for \(x\):

\( \displaystyle {@a*x@} - {@b@} \ge {@c*x@} + {@d@} \)

(Enter your answer as an inequality. Use >= for \(\ge\). Leave any decimals as simplified fractions.)

Inequality: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Based on your solution, what is the smallest integer value of \(x\) that makes this inequality true?

\(x = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part (a): Solving the Inequality

First, we group the terms with \(x\) on the left side and the constant terms on the right side.

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@a*x@} - {@c*x@} &\ge {@d@} + {@b@} \\ {@a - c@}x &\ge {@d + b@} \\ x &\ge \frac{{@d + b@}}{{@a - c@}} \end{aligned} \)

If we evaluate the fraction, we get \( x \ge {@disp_dec@} \).

Hence, the simplified inequality is:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{x \ge {@frac@}} \)

Part (b): Smallest Integer

The inequality states that \(x\) must be greater than or equal to \({@disp_dec@}\). The integers that are greater than \({@disp_dec@}\) are \({@ta2@}, {@ta2+1@}, {@ta2+2@}, \dots\)

Hence, the smallest integer in this set is:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@ta2@}} \)

On a number line the solution starts at \({@frac@}\) (closed circle) and goes to the right; the first whole number on it is \({@ta2@}\).

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on the example 3x - 9 < 6 + x (collecting terms on one side) in the section Simple Inequalities of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Simple Inequalities (Variables Both Sides & Integer Limits)

truefeedback.text: You rounded the decimal down. However, the inequality states that \(x\) must be greater than or equal to the fraction. The integer \({@wrong_int@}\) is less than the fraction, so it does not satisfy the inequality. You need the next integer up.
